display.title: Reb Gavriel and the Pirates
display.summary_short: Shipwrecked on an island, Reb Gavriel stumbles into a pirates' hideout, and his trust in Hashem turns a death sentence into a long-lost student's return.
display.summary_long: Reb Gavriel keeps learning Torah while a storm wrecks his ship, holding on to the Tzemach Tzedek's words, 'Think good and it will be good.' He floats on a plank to an island, washes negel vasser (with a lesson on washing after a daytime nap), and follows smoke to a hidden house under the ground, full of food. He eats only fruit he knows is kosher, after making brachos, and the storyteller explains why eating without a brachah is like taking from the Beis HaMikdash. He falls asleep on a couch, and a band of pirates returns to its hideout and finds him. Their captain threatens him with a sword and gives him five minutes for a last prayer, while Reb Gavriel wonders, with the Baal Shem Tov's teaching on hashgachah pratis, why Hashem brought him there. Then the captain looks into his eyes and goes pale: he is Moshe, a Jewish boy Reb Gavriel once taught in Smolensk, who drifted away. In tears he asks how he can do teshuvah. That night they escape with the stolen money to a Rav, the robbers are arrested, and Moshe returns to Torah and becomes a talmid chacham.
display.lesson: Trust in Hashem and think good, even in danger; everything happens for a reason, and it is never too late to do teshuvah.
